query: My former software employer is threatening legal action claiming I cannot join another IT firm due to a 2-year non-compete clause in my offer letter.

model_output.summary: Your former employer is threatening legal action over a 2-year non-compete clause in your offer letter. In India, agreements that stop someone from doing a lawful job or business are generally void and unenforceable.
facts_extracted: Former employer is a software firm
Threat is based on a 2-year non-compete clause in the offer letter
You intend to join another IT firm

options.title: Consult District Legal Services Authority (DLSA)
options.description: Reach out to your local DLSA or call the NALSA Helpline 15100 to check if you qualify for free legal advice or representation.
cons: May have eligibility criteria based on income or employment status

options.title: Respond through an Advocate
options.description: Have an advocate reply to your former employer pointing out that post-employment non-compete clauses are void under Indian law.

citations.relevance: Applies to post-employment non-compete clauses, stating that agreements restraining someone from exercising a lawful profession are generally void.
Outlines eligibility criteria for receiving free legal services and advice from the DLSA or NALSA.

model_output.lawyer_reason: Since your former employer is threatening legal action, it is important to have an advocate respond properly and protect you against any court summons.
missing_info: Whether any formal legal notice or court summons has already been delivered to you
Whether you received any special compensation or training during your employment tied to the clause
